rationale: This study is a technical/metrological engineering and utility revenue-loss investigation rather than a study of household water service access. Using pilot-scale and laboratory-scale tests, the authors evaluate how water meter metrological class (Class B vs. Class C) and meter age affect meter under-registration (apparent water losses) and assess the economic viability of meter replacement for Brazilian water utilities. Tariff policy and household water tanks are only discussed ('discoursed out about') regarding utility financial performance and water consumption, and no household service access, connection, reliability, affordability, or exclusion outcome is empirically evaluated.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings yield exclude. Although the abstract notes that the authors 'discoursed out about' tariff policy in relation to utility financial performance and user consumption, the empirical investigation itself is a pilot- and laboratory-scale engineering/metrological study of Class B versus Class C water meters aimed at reducing utility apparent water losses and revenue under-registration, rather than examining household water service access outcomes.

evidence_quotes.quote: in this study was evaluated the influence of metrological class and the usage time of meters on under-registration, through study on pilot scale and tests in a laboratory scale.
Thus, was proven significant reduction of apparent water losses due to the replacement of class B meters by the class C meters, and the economic viability of this investment.
Furthermore, discoursed out about the interference of the use of water tanks and about the influence of tariff policy on the financial performance of the utilities and consumption of users.
